items.stem: Explain the sliding filament theory of muscle contraction with a diagram.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between tetany and myasthenia gravis on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A disorder of the muscular or skeletal system is described: may cause paralysis of skeletal muscle. Identify the disorder – tetany or myasthenia gravis? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Tetany: rapid spasms in muscle; wild contractions; due to low Ca²⁺ in body fluid. Myasthenia gravis: autoimmune disorder; affects the neuromuscular junction; leads to fatigue and weakening. (b) Myasthenia gravis.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: myasthenia gravis; 1 mark: “may cause paralysis of skeletal muscle” is a feature of myasthenia gravis.

items.stem: Distinguish between skeletal muscle and visceral muscle on any three points.
items.answer: Skeletal muscle: striated appearance; voluntary control; involved in locomotion and changes of body posture. Visceral muscle: located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs; helps transport food through the digestive tract and gametes through the genital tract; smooth (non-striated).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. skeletal muscle – striated appearance; voluntary control; involved in locomotion and changes of body posture; visceral muscle – located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs; helps transport food through the digestive tract and gametes through the genital tract; smooth (non-striated).

items.stem: Explain the term “axial skeleton”.
items.answer: The 80 bones distributed along the main axis of the body: skull, vertebral column, sternum and ribs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the 80 bones distributed along the main axis of the body: skull, vertebral column, sternum and ribs.

items.stem: Which of the following is an example of ciliary movement?
items.answer: removal of dust in the trachea
items.markingKey: (a) Removal of dust in the trachea is an example of ciliary movement; the others are not.
options: removal of dust in the trachea
movement of tongue
leucocytes in blood
movement of jaws

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the mechanism of muscle contraction is incorrect?
items.answer: During contraction the A-band shortens.
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “During contraction the A-band shortens.” Correct form: The A-band length remains constant; the I-band and H-zone shorten.
options: Ca²⁺ ions are pumped back to the sarcoplasmic reticulum, which masks the actin filaments and causes relaxation.
Increase in Ca²⁺ level leads to binding of calcium with troponin on actin filaments.
The H-zone shortens or disappears during contraction.
During contraction the A-band shortens.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as example of ciliary movement or example of amoeboid movement: macrophages, leucocytes in blood, passage of ova through the female reproductive tract.
items.answer: macrophages – example of amoeboid movement; leucocytes in blood – example of amoeboid movement; passage of ova through the female reproductive tract – example of ciliary movement.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: macrophages – example of amoeboid movement; leucocytes in blood – example of amoeboid movement; passage of ova through the female reproductive tract – example of ciliary movement.

items.stem: Which term describes movement by cilia, which occurs in most internal tubular organs lined by ciliated epithelium?
items.answer: ciliary movement
items.markingKey: (a) Ciliary movement: movement by cilia, which occurs in most internal tubular organs lined by ciliated epithelium.
options: ciliary movement
sarcolemma
meromyosin
sarcoplasmic reticulum

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Gout is due to accumulation of urea in joints.”
items.answer: Gout is inflammation of joints due to accumulation of uric acid crystals.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Gout is inflammation of joints due to accumulation of uric acid crystals.

items.stem:
A muscle type is described: voluntary control; closely associated with skeletal components; striated appearance.
(i) Identify the muscle type. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were cardiac muscle? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Skeletal muscle (ii) involved in locomotion and changes of body posture (iii) involuntary; muscles of the heart
items.markingKey: (i) skeletal muscle – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: involved in locomotion and changes of body posture – 1 mark. (iii) for cardiac muscle: muscles of the heart; striated; involuntary – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: A region of the sarcomere is described during contraction: bisected by the Z-line; light band. Identify the region. Give a reason.
items.answer: The I-band
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the I-band; 1 mark: the features bisected by the Z-line; light band are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Arthritis is the inflammation of muscles.
Reason (R): The skull has 22 bones: 8 cranial and 14 facial bones.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Arthritis is the inflammation of joints. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of events in muscle contraction: Ca²⁺ released from sarcoplasmic reticulum, action potential in the sarcolemma, neural signal reaches the neuromuscular junction, acetylcholine released. Give a reason.
items.answer: neural signal reaches the neuromuscular junction → acetylcholine released → action potential in the sarcolemma → Ca²⁺ released from sarcoplasmic reticulum
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order neural signal reaches the neuromuscular junction → acetylcholine released → action potential in the sarcolemma → Ca²⁺ released from sarcoplasmic reticulum; 1 mark for the reason: Excitation-contraction coupling.

items.stem: A muscle type is described: muscles of the heart; striated. Identify the muscle type. Give a reason.
items.answer: Cardiac muscle
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cardiac muscle; 1 mark: the features muscles of the heart; striated are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a bone of the appendicular skeleton?
items.answer: sternum
items.markingKey: (b) Sternum is a bone of the axial skeleton, not a bone of the appendicular skeleton.
options: pelvic bones
sternum
scapula
clavicle

items.stem: Which term describes the link formed when the myosin head binds to the exposed active site on actin?
items.answer: cross bridge
items.markingKey: (c) Cross bridge: the link formed when the myosin head binds to the exposed active site on actin.
options: muscle fatigue
motor unit
cross bridge
sliding filament theory

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Thick filaments slide over thin filaments towards the Z-line.”
items.answer: Thin (actin) filaments slide towards the centre of the A-band, pulling the Z-lines inward.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Thin (actin) filaments slide towards the centre of the A-band, pulling the Z-lines inward.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Muscle is a specialised tissue of mesodermal origin.
Reason (R): The light band contains myosin and is called the A-band.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The light I-band contains actin; the dark A-band contains myosin.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A disorder of the muscular or skeletal system is described: progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle; mostly due to a genetic disorder. Identify the disorder. Give a reason.
items.answer: Muscular dystrophy
items.markingKey: 1 mark: muscular dystrophy; 1 mark: the features progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle; mostly due to a genetic disorder are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
A region of the sarcomere is described during contraction: length remains the same during contraction; contains thick myosin filaments; dark band.
(i) Identify the region. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the I-band? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The A-band (ii) anisotropic (iii) light band; shortens during contraction
items.markingKey: (i) the A-band – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: anisotropic – 1 mark. (iii) for the I-band: shortens during contraction; contains only thin actin filaments; light band – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the skeletal system, joints and disorders of the muscular and skeletal systems is correct?
items.answer: Each limb has 30 bones.
items.markingKey: (b) Each limb has 30 bones. The other statements are false. The skull has 22 bones; each limb has 30 bones. Gout is inflammation of joints due to accumulation of uric acid crystals. Arthritis is the inflammation of joints.
options: Arthritis is the inflammation of muscles.
Each limb has 30 bones.
Gout is due to accumulation of urea in joints.
The human skull has 30 bones.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between muscular dystrophy and tetany on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A disorder of the muscular or skeletal system is described: wild contractions. Identify the disorder – muscular dystrophy or tetany? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Muscular dystrophy: progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle; mostly due to a genetic disorder; muscle weakness increases with time. Tetany: rapid spasms in muscle; wild contractions; due to low Ca²⁺ in body fluid. (b) Tetany.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: tetany; 1 mark: “wild contractions” is a feature of tetany.

items.stem: Compare skeletal muscle and visceral muscle on any three points.
items.answer: Skeletal muscle: involved in locomotion and changes of body posture; voluntary control; closely associated with skeletal components. Visceral muscle: smooth (non-striated); helps transport food through the digestive tract and gametes through the genital tract; involuntary.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. skeletal muscle – involved in locomotion and changes of body posture; voluntary control; closely associated with skeletal components; visceral muscle – smooth (non-striated); helps transport food through the digestive tract and gametes through the genital tract; involuntary.

items.stem: Explain the term “synovial joints”.
items.answer: Joints with a fluid-filled synovial cavity between the articulating surfaces that allow considerable movement.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: joints with a fluid-filled synovial cavity between the articulating surfaces that allow considerable movement.

items.stem: Which of the following is an example of muscular movement?
items.answer: movement of limbs
items.markingKey: (a) Movement of limbs is an example of muscular movement; the others are not.
options: movement of limbs
leucocytes in blood
passage of ova through the female reproductive tract
removal of dust in the trachea

items.answer: Muscle fatigue is due to accumulation of urea.

options: Muscle fatigue is due to accumulation of urea.
The myosin head hydrolyses ATP and uses the energy to bind to the exposed active site on actin.
